name: SNAPPY
summary: SNAPPY is a launched CubeSat technology demonstrator for space-based solar-neutrino detection. It tests detector operation and background signatures in orbit to support possible future missions closer to the Sun; launch does not by itself demonstrate neutrino detection.
detection_principle: A compact scintillation detector studies charged-particle and gamma backgrounds and the double-pulse signature expected from gallium neutrino-capture reactions. Its present role is flight qualification and background measurement.

sites.name: Low Earth orbit
sites.location: Orbital detector; not a fixed terrestrial site

status.label: Operating / data taking
status.evidence: NASA confirms launch on 3 May 2026. Wichita State reports detector activation and first data on 4 August and full-power downloads on 21 August; these are detector and background data, not a claimed solar-neutrino discovery.

key_parameters.name: Mission role
key_parameters.value: Detector flight qualification and interaction-signature background measurements

results.summary: NASA confirms launch on 3 May 2026. Wichita State reports detector activation and first data on 4 August and full-power downloads on 21 August; these are detector and background data, not a claimed solar-neutrino discovery.

science_scope: The orbital demonstrator and a future near-Sun neutrino observatory are different mission stages. The cited reports do not claim that solar neutrinos have been identified in flight.
